metadata.title: Health Literacy and Communication in Stroke Prevention, Management, and Recovery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
top_takeaways: Health literacy is strongly associated with functional outcomes and stroke-related morbidity across the entire stroke care continuum, yet patient capacity is often exceeded by communication demands.

Nurse-led interprofessional interventions—such as teach-back-based education, dyadic psychoeducational programs, and tailored digital support—effectively improve stroke knowledge, self-efficacy, quality of life, and caregiver preparedness.

Healthcare organizations must prioritize standardized health literacy assessments, workforce training in plain-language and culturally responsive communication, and equitable implementation of emerging digital technologies.

recommendations.statement: Nurse-led and interprofessional care interventions, including teach-back-based education, dyadic psychoeducational programs, and tailored digital support, should be implemented across stroke care systems to enhance stroke knowledge, self-efficacy, quality of life, and caregiver preparedness.
recommendations.loe_label: Moderate-quality evidence from nonrandomized or heterogenous studies
recommendations.target_population: Patients with stroke and their caregivers, including those with stroke-related cognitive or language impairments
